/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 14 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3445 (-62)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5912 (-168)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2393 (-14)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1725 (6)
Baltic Handysize Index: 942 (2)
CAPESIZE
A rather subdued start to the week, with the BCI 182 5TC falling $1,517 to $53,622. The Pacific was a touch softer, with the C5 index easing $0.590 to $17.255, while C3 was effectively unchanged, dipping just $0.005 to $42.118. Activity was limited across the Atlantic, with a typical Monday feel as market participants assessed direction. South Brazil and West Africa to China were generally viewed as having some potential to nudge higher, with talk of $42.50 being concluded at the end of last week for forward dates and offers said to be approaching $43. In the Pacific, just one C5 miner was in the market, opening bids around $16.80 against offers in the upper $17s. By the close, $17.20, and $17.15 had been concluded, reflecting the relatively narrow spread that developed through the session. Overall, it was a quiet opening to the week, with limited activity.
PANAMAX
The trans-Atlantic market saw mixed sentiment today, with most participants agreeing that both Owners and Charterers approached the start of the week cautiously. Many appeared to be keeping their distance while attempting to gauge any clear market direction. As a result, reports suggested a wide bid-offer spread, with overall activity described as relatively subdued. By contrast, firmer demand for fronthaul business from the US Gulf was said to be providing some support to overall sentiment, despite the cautious tone seen elsewhere in the market resulting in the P2A marking a slight increase today. Activity in the Pacific has eased compared with last week, with fewer fixtures reported. Mirroring sentiment in the Atlantic basin, many market participants appear to be taking a step back to assess their positions and gain a clearer view of market direction before adjusting pricing expectations. The P5TC dropped today by $122 to conclude at $21,540.
SUPRAMAX
The usual subdued start to a week, with most collecting and assessing, but the 11TC average rose $79 to open the week at $21,807. The Eptalofos (61,156 2023) Cai Lan 17-20 September fixed short period with Marla (1st leg cement to Houston) at $22,750, although early reports incorrectly linked the Charterer with the Genco Magic which remained open according to sources. The Pacific Valor (63,564 2015) Bohai Bay 17 Sep fixed a trip via Gulf of Aden to the Mediterranean in the mid $23,000’s and the Thor Friendship (54,123 2010 OHBS) prompt CJK did a trip Singapore with cement at $19,000, but in both cases the Charterer was unknown. The Bi Jia Shan (56,625 2012) Mombasa end September fixed to Bainbridge via South Africa to East coast India with iron ore redelivery Singapore at $16,500, the Desert Challenger (61,259 2017) Chittagong 15 September was said to have fixed to Oldendorff at close to $19,000 for a trip via Indonesia back to India and the Desert Pioneer (60,980 2022) prompt Chittagong fixed a similar trip with Tongli at $19,500 brokers said.
HANDYSIZE
The week opened on a quiet but relatively healthy note, with the BHSI increasing by 2 points to 942 and the 7TC average gaining $34 to settle at $16,959. The Continent and Mediterranean maintained a balanced outlook, with rates holding steady. A 40,000-dwt was reported fixed via ARAG to Sweden at $17,500 by Trithorn, although further details were not disclosed. The South Atlantic remained broadly unchanged, with prompt positions continuing to clear and rates holding around last-done levels. Meanwhile, the US Gulf continued to gain momentum, with rates firming despite limited reported fixtures and little fresh information. Across Asia, the market remained subdued. Demand continued to lag, while sources pointed to a slightly extended tonnage list, contributing to the overall soft sentiment.

Market Fundamentals
Bayan Resources Declares Force Majeure

One of Indonesia’s lowest-cost coal producers, Bayan Resources, announced force majeure on contracts from October, McCloskey reports. The company attributed the default to a supply deficit in a notice to buyers dated 11 September, as it awaits Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) approval for increased 2026 production quotas. The ESDM approved an RKAB allowing 39.0 Mt of production quotas in February for Bayan, falling short of the 76.0 Mt the company had sought. The miner produced 68.0 Mt of coal in 2025 and is expanding infrastructure to support a targeted production capacity of 80mtpa.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape was sharply weaker today across the curve. September traded from 51,000 early before sliding steadily to 49,000 later in the session. October was the main focus, opening around 48,000–48,250 and weakening through 47,500, 46,750 and eventually 46,000, before a small late recovery to 46,500. November softened from 45,000 to around 44,100–44,250, while December traded down from 43,250 to 42,500. Q4 26 moved from 45,750 early to 44,000–44,500 late. Q1 27 also came under pressure, falling from around 31,000 to 30,000–30,250. Cal 27 weakened from 33,600 to 32,900. Overall, the session was heavily offered, with sustained selling pressure across the front end and nearby quarters.

PMX
PMX started the week on a softer tone across the curve. September eased from 22,000 early to 21,600 later in the session. October saw the heaviest activity, initially trading up to 23,500 before coming under sustained pressure and falling through 23,000 to around 22,300 late on. November moved from 23,000 down to 22,150–22,200, while December weakened from around 21,800 to 21,500. Q4 26 followed the same direction, dropping from 22,800 early to 21,950–22,000 by the close. Q1 27 traded from 18,350 early before sliding to around 17,900–18,000. Q2 27 softened from around 19,200 to 19,000, while Cal 27 fell from 18,500 to 18,000.

SMX + HANDY
The smx market lost support to start the week. October opened at 21,300 before steadily weakening through 21,000 during the morning and trading mainly around 20,750–20,800 in the afternoon. November moved from 20,850 early to around 20,750–20,800, while December traded mainly around 20,000 before briefly dipping to 19,950. Q4 26 saw good activity, falling from 21,000 early to 20,600 by late morning and reaching 20,500 during the afternoon, before finishing around 20,600. Q1 27 traded between 16,300–16,450, while Cal 27 printed at 16,250.
